correctness.rationale: Correct as stated for fixed r>=3 and finite induced A in the countable homogeneous K_r-free Henson graph. Proof reconstructs QE/homogeneity, the exact permitted S subset criterion, extension over A and infinite multiplicity of each outside type, giving Theta=C_{r-1} and total n+C(1). #P membership uses unique witness tags; joining arbitrary bipartite B with K_{r-3} is K_r-free and yields the exact offset for a polynomial-time metric reduction from exact bipartite #IS. Checked r=3, empty join, empty parameter set, and the five-point examples. Independent bounded enumeration tested 3,672 permissible parameter graphs and 112,580 one-point neighborhood masks, plus 3,445 bipartite-join identities across fixed r=3..7. Finite testing was not treated as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Finite complete 1-type spaces are a canonical invariant of the Henson free-amalgamation theories, and the coefficient polynomial records all neighborhood sizes rather than only an isolated numerical count. The exact computational-complexity classification identifies a genuine tractability barrier for a natural model-theoretic counting problem, uniformly for every fixed clique prohibition r; the explicit bipartite join gadget is a reusable reduction despite its short proof. This is not intrinsically just a rebranding of the independence polynomial: the natural object to count is complete 1-types, and the r-dependent restriction and uniform hardness require an explicit bridge. The previously known r=3 admissibility rule by itself would not suffice to establish a new independent result, and this value assessment attaches to the full exact-complexity theorem. No downstream theorem or paper-sized contribution is required.
sources: Assigned RESULT.md complete final theorem and metric-reduction proof

final_claim: For every fixed r>=3 and finite induced parameter graph A in the Henson K_r-free graph, the nonalgebraic complete 1-type neighborhood-size enumerator equals C_{r-1}(A;y), with n additional algebraic types; exact total finite-parameter 1-type counting is #P-complete under polynomial-time metric reductions, even on A=B join K_{r-3} for bipartite B.
